name: ctrlc
description: ^C at a bsh prompt is an INTERRUPT, not a character.  A nested `sh` is started (it must OUTLIVE the injection, or the harness ends the run at the first returned prompt), a raw $03 is injected at frame 400, and `pwd` is typed at frame 900 with NO Enter in between -- so the two share one line buffer.  If the $03 was inserted as data the shell runs '<^C>pwd', which fails; if it was consumed as SIGINT the buffer is empty and pwd prints /root.  /root cannot come from anywhere else here: the nested shell's prompt is '#' and the outer one is 'fgx#'.  The screen_lacks list is the other half, and 'cannot execute' is in it because that is what bsh ACTUALLY says for '<^C>pwd' -- the mutation run printed it while 'not found' stayed clean, so asserting only the latter would have caught nothing -- it catches the shell trying to EXECUTE a command with a control byte glued to its front.  Avoid quotes in post_commands; they do not survive the paste, which cost a run that looked like a kernel failure.  GOES RED WITHOUT THE FIX: FGX never ran 2.11BSD ttyopen()'s process-group half (tty.c:650-660), so tty[0] had no foreground group; the heartbeat converts ^C to SIGINT only for a line that HAS one, and with none the raw $03 reached the shell as ordinary input.  Compared against real BSD, where ^C on an empty sh line echoes and returns a fresh prompt.  Control-verified: with no injection the screen shows ONE '#', with it TWO -- the second is the interrupt's fresh prompt.
